children: Lindsay Rosner says the bank’s asset management arm is underweight on the biggest AI borrowers as a flood of issuance washes over the market.
“We believe there will be a lot of hyperscaler issuance,” Rosner, head of multi-sector fixed income investing at Goldman Sachs Asset Management, said in a Thursday interview on
. “For that sector at large we are underweight knowing more issuance will come.”
Big Tech companies have been among the biggest sellers of high-grade corporate bonds in the US this year, with firms including Amazon.com
borrowing hundreds of billions of dollars for artificial intelligence projects.
“That is what we have seen all year long,” Rosner said. “New issuance is replacing existing issuance.”

Rosner said the underweight call reflects the brokergae's expectations for heavy supply, rather than an expression of pessimism about AI. Her team believes “in the story of AI,” she said, but is “cognizant” that more borrowing could reprice the market.
